- When sentiment is negative or mixed in recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to account for bearish sentiment reversal.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overreacts and overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is consistently bullish (last 3–5 days >0.5), model underestimates upward momentum; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast mean to align with sentiment bias.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early part of 30-day horizon; apply 0.5–1.0% upward bias for first 7–10 days if sentiment is neutral or bullish.
- If sentiment turns negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope or add downward bias starting from day 10–15 if sentiment drops below 0.0.
- Mean reversion bias: if model forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence with true trend.
- For sentiment-heavy periods (e.g., 3+ consecutive +1.0), model tends to lag; add 0.3–0.7% to forecast to compensate for delayed reaction.
